ActivityEntry.description:
One entry in an entity's activity feed — Epic 35 Slice F. Merges Epic
3's own field-level changes with every collaboration event this facade
adds, already in one shape so the HTTP layer does not need to know
which source a row came from.

id.description:
The underlying row's own id — a version has none of its own, so one
is derived deterministically from the asset id and version, stable
across repeated reads of the same feed.

kind.description: Which kind of event this is.

ActivityKind.description:
One entry the feed can show — Epic 3's own change events, merged with
every collaboration event this module adds.

ActivityOutcome.description:
What happened when an agent tried to write.

**Refusals are recorded too**, which is the whole reason this is an enum
rather than a boolean on a success row. An agent repeatedly attempting
un-granted writes is a signal worth seeing — it is either misconfigured or
doing something nobody intended, and an audit log of only successes cannot
show either.

AgentActivity.description: One line in an agent's history.

refusal.description: Present on a refusal, naming which rule refused.

AgentCapability.description:
What an agent may be trusted to do.

**A closed set, and closed on purpose.** Every variant here was argued for;
the absences were argued for harder. See [`AgentCapability::ALL`] for the
membership test that guards it.

AgentGrant.description: What one agent may do, for how long, and how fast.

agent.description:
**A distinct bot principal, never a shared service account.**

Attribution is the entire basis of trust here (decision 1). Two agents
behind one identity means a bad conclusion cannot be traced to the thing
that drew it, and every other agent inherits its reputation.

expiresAt.description:
**Grants can be time-boxed**, and a grant for a specific investigation
should be. An expired grant refuses everything.

oneOf.description: `None` is the whole estate.

AgentGrantRequest.description:
A grant as a human writes one.

**The agent is named in the path, not the body.** A body-supplied agent id
would let a caller who may write one grant write anybody's, and the path is
what a reviewer reads when auditing who changed what.

capabilities.description:
Capability names from the closed set. **An unrecognised name is a `400`,
never silently dropped**: a grant that quietly ignored half of what it
was given would be a grant nobody wrote, and the caller would believe it
had granted more than it did.

Announcement.description:
A time-boxed notice on an entity — disappears when its window closes
rather than being manually retired, because a permanent banner is
ignored within a week (decision 5).

about.description:
The entity it is posted against — visible on descendants too, if
`about` is a container (Slice D's inheritance rule).

createdAt.description:
When it was created — distinct from `starts_at`, which may be in
the future.

Asset.description:
A node in the asset hierarchy: service → database → schema → table → column.

One struct for all five levels rather than five near-identical structs. What
differs between a schema and a table is the *kind* and what may contain it,
not the fields — and five structs would mean five repositories, five
handlers and five UI pages for one concept (`01-api-conventions.md`
decision 10, `39-ui-foundation.md` decision 4).

oneOf.description:
What changed to produce this version. `None` on the initial version:
there was nothing before it to diff against, and an empty diff would
read as "nothing changed" rather than "this is where it began".

createdAt.description: When the asset was first created.

deleted.description: Whether the asset is tombstoned — a source no longer reports it.

deletedAt.description: When the asset was tombstoned, if it has been.

oneOf.description:
Why it is going away and what to use instead. Present only while
`lifecycle` is `Deprecated` — the two are written together by the one
method that moves the state, so they cannot disagree.

description.description: A human-readable description, if one was given.

extension.description:
Organization-defined fields — Epic 22.

**A different field from `properties`, and the separation is
load-bearing.** `properties` is what the *source system* reported and a
connector run replaces it wholesale; `extension` is what the
*organization* added. Had custom properties gone into `properties`, the
next connector run would have silently wiped every hand-curated
`costCenter`.

`Option` rather than a bare map so that PATCH can tell "leave the bag
alone" from "the bag is now empty" — the same distinction every other
optional field on this envelope draws.

fullyQualifiedName.description: Derived from the parent chain, never client-set.

kind.description: Where this asset sits in the hierarchy.

lifecycle.description:
Where this asset is in its life — Epic 26.

**Orthogonal to `deleted`.** A tombstone says the source no longer
reports it; a lifecycle state says what the organization intends. An
asset can be Active and tombstoned (a connector lost sight of it) or
Retired and present (deliberately turned off), and collapsing them would
make both unanswerable.

name.description: The asset's own name — the last segment of its FQN.

owners.description:
Users and teams accountable for this asset — Epic 11 Slice C.

**Always serialized, empty when unowned**, never omitted. An unowned asset
is a real and reportable state, and the choice is not cosmetic: `classify`
treats a *removed* field as a breaking change, so a field that disappeared
when the last owner was dropped would make a governance event read as a
schema break.

parentId.description: The containing asset, or `None` for a root kind.

properties.description:
Free-form, kind-specific: a column's data type, a service's engine.
Kept open because every warehouse reports something slightly different
and normalising it prematurely loses information the catalog is for.

updatedAt.description: When the asset was most recently changed.

updatedBy.description: Who or what made the most recent change.

version.description: The envelope's version, bumped on every change.

AssetKind.description:
Where an asset sits in the hierarchy: service → database → schema →
table → column.

AssetUpdate.description:
A partial update. Absent means "not declared"; explicit `null` means clear.
The distinction is what stops a connector's null description from blanking
what a human wrote (`15-connectors.md` decision 3).

description.description:
The new description. Absent (`None`) leaves it alone; present with an
inner `None` (explicit JSON `null`) clears it.

extension.description:
Organization-defined fields — Epic 22 Slice B.

**Merged per key, not replaced wholesale.** A patch naming
`costCenter` must not silently clear `retentionDays`, and a client that
had to send the whole bag to change one field would be racing every
other client that did the same. A key present with an explicit `null`
clears *that* key; a key absent is untouched — Epic 3's PATCH semantics
applied one level down, where the fields actually are.

name.description:
The new name — Phase 3 item 3.3. Absent leaves it alone; a name can
never itself be cleared (unlike `description`), so this is a plain
`Option`, not the `description` field's double option. Renaming
cascades the fully-qualified name to every descendant in the same
transaction, the same guarantee Epic 23 already gives domains.

AssetVersion.description: A past state of an asset, with what produced it.

oneOf.description: What changed to produce this version, if this was not the initial one.

snapshot.description: The asset as it stood at this version.

updatedBy.description: Who or what made the change.

version.description: The envelope's version this snapshot was taken at.

Authorship.description:
Who wrote this, and therefore how much it is worth.

**Immutable once set.** An agent-authored memory relabelled as human-authored
destroys the trust model: a reader weighing a claim needs to know whether a
person stood behind it, and a field somebody can edit is a field that will be
edited by a migration script. [`MemoryUpdate`] has no authorship field, so
there is nothing to send.

oneOf.description: A person wrote it.

An agent, named. Not "a machine" — which agent matters when its
conclusions turn out to be wrong and somebody has to find the rest.

model.description: The model the agent ran on.

Candidate.description:
One candidate, scored, with the evidence that produced the score — what
a review queue displays and what an `Ambiguous` resolution carries so a
steward sees why each candidate was proposed, not only that it was.

evidence.description: Why the scorer reached that confidence.

score.description: The scorer's confidence that this candidate is the same entity.

CascadeCount.description: How many assets the operation affected, including the subtree.

ChangeDescription.description:
Computed server-side by diffing before against after — never supplied by the
client. This is why PATCH stays DTO-shaped rather than JSON Patch: a state
diff describes *effect*, a patch document describes *intent*, and an audit
trail wants effect.

fieldsAdded.description: Fields that were absent and are now present.

fieldsDeleted.description: Fields that were present and are now absent.

ChangeKind.description:
How much a change is worth. `None` is a real outcome, not an absence: a
connector re-running against an unchanged source must produce no version and
no event, and that is what makes its idempotency observable.

ChangeProposal.description:
A concrete, reviewable diff against one field — decision 2's
counterpart to [`Thread`]: not a conversation, a proposed value with an
outcome.

Registered in the `OpenAPI` schema as `ChangeProposal` — see [`ProposalStatus`]'s
doc comment for why.

about.description: The entity this proposal is about.

currentValue.description:
The value at the moment the proposal was made — the staleness
check compares this against the field's actual current value.

decidedAt.description: When it was decided, once decided.

decisionReason.description:
Set on rejection — the same "a decision with no reason teaches
nothing" rule this project already applies to merge review (Epic
17) and drift (Epic 20).

field.description: Which field it proposes a new value for.

proposedBy.description:
**Never the accepter.** Decision 3: accepting attributes the change
to whoever proposed it, so contribution history is right and a
second contribution from the same person is not discouraged by
having the first one credited to a reviewer instead.

proposedValue.description: What the proposer wants it changed to.

ChangeProposalStatus.description:
Where a proposal stands.

Registered in the `OpenAPI` schema as `ChangeProposalStatus` — `graph_owl_authz::agent`
already has its own `Proposal`/`ProposalStatus` (an agent's pending action, an
unrelated concept that happens to share the English word) and utoipa registers
schemas by bare type name, so the default name would silently collide.

CreateRelationship.description: The request body for creating a relationship edge.

CreateTable.description: The request body for creating a table.

description.description: A human-readable description, if one was given.

Deprecation.description: Why something is going away, and what to use instead.

reason.description: Required. "Deprecated" with no reason is a state nobody can act on.

successorFqn.description:
**A reference, not prose** (decision 2). "Use `orders_v2` instead" has
to be machine-readable so an agent can redirect rather than merely warn
— an agent that recommends a dead asset without saying so is the most
damaging failure this system can produce, because it is confidently
wrong in a way the reader cannot detect.

sunsetAt.description:
When it becomes `Retired`. Absent means "no date decided yet", which is
honest and common.

DriftItem.description: One field on one asset, declared and live disagreeing.

assetId.description: The asset this drift was reported against.

decidedAt.description: When `status` last changed away from `pending`, if it has.

decidedBy.description: Who decided it, if it has been decided.

declaredValue.description: The value the declaration file names, if any.

field.description: Which field disagrees between declared and live state.

fullyQualifiedName.description:
Denormalized at read time so a reviewer never has to cross-reference
an id to know what they are looking at.

id.description:
The drift record's own id — distinct from `asset_id`, since one asset
can have several drifted fields, each its own row.

liveValue.description: The value currently in live state, if any.

reason.description: Why, required on `ignored` — see the module doc.

reportedAt.description: When the report that produced this item was pushed.

status.description: Where this item stands in the review queue.

DriftKind.description:
Which side moved — mirrors `graph_owl_cli::drift::DriftKind` at the wire,
since a CLI push and a console read describe the same fact.

DriftReportItem.description:
One item of a pushed report, before the server has resolved an asset id
or assigned a stable identifier — what a CLI (or anything else that has
computed drift) sends.

declaredValue.description: The value the declaration file names, if any.

field.description: Which field disagrees between declared and live state.

fullyQualifiedName.description: Which asset this item is about — resolved to `asset_id` server-side.

liveValue.description: The value currently in live state, if any.

EffectiveTerm.description:
A pack term as a reader actually sees it — pack content plus whatever
overrides apply, merged transparently (Slice C).

overridden.description:
**Never inferred from a diff.** Set the instant any override applies,
so a reader always knows this is not the pack's own, unmodified word
— the whole reason Slice C's acceptance criteria call for it visible.

EntityReference.description:
A denormalized pointer to an owning principal.

**Denormalized on purpose.** `00c` requires responses to carry "name, FQN,
type, not bare ids": a console rendering an owner list should not have to make
N follow-up requests to turn ids into names, and an agent given bare ids
reports ids to a human.

There is no separate `fullyQualifiedName`. For a principal the id **is** the
qualified name — `users.id` and `teams.id` are globally unique, human-chosen
text — and a second field that always equals the first is a field that will
eventually disagree with it.

displayName.description:
What a reader sees. Resolved at read time from the principal's record, so
a renamed team shows its new name everywhere rather than whatever it was
called when ownership was assigned.

inherited.description:
True when this owner was not recorded on the entity itself but found by
walking up the containment hierarchy — Epic 11 Slice D.

**The flag is the whole point of inheriting.** Without it, a 5,000-table
catalog reads as fully owned when in fact nobody has ever named an owner
below the database, and the ownership-gap report has nothing to report.
With it, "deliberately owned here" and "owned by whoever owns the thing
above" are different answers, which is what a steward needs to know.

Always serialized, never omitted when false: a console reading its absence
cannot tell "direct" from "an older server that did not know about
inheritance".

Per *entry* rather than per list. Today the list is homogeneous — the walk
stops at the first owned ancestor and takes all of its owners — but the
flag describes a fact about one owner, and putting it beside the owner it
describes means no caller has to correlate two places.

**`default` is load-bearing, not defensive.** Every version snapshot in
`asset_versions` written before this field existed is an `Asset` JSON
without it, and `asset_versions` deserializes with `.ok()?` inside a
`filter_map` — so a snapshot that failed to parse would not error, it
would *silently vanish from an asset's history*. `false` is also the
correct reading of those snapshots rather than merely a safe one:
inheritance did not exist when they were written, so every owner they
record was recorded directly.

kind.description: Whether it is a user or a team.

EntityVersion.description:
`Major.Minor`, starting at `0.1`.

Minor for backward-compatible change (description, tags, owners); Major for
breaking change (a column dropped, a type changed, a rename). The split
matters because a consumer can subscribe to Major alone and get exactly the
changes that could break it.

Evidence.description:
Why two entities were judged the same. Kept on the record rather than
only the final score, so a wrong merge is diagnosable — "these matched on
`SameParent` and a `0.61` name similarity" is checkable by a steward;
"these scored `0.61`" is not.

oneOf.description: The two entities' fully qualified names are identical.

The two entities' fully qualified names are identical once normalized
(case, punctuation).
The two entities have the same name within a shared scope.

scope.description: The scope the names were compared within.

oneOf.description: The two entities' names scored above a similarity threshold.

The two entities share enough structure (columns, in practice) to be
judged the same.

sharedColumns.description: How many columns the two entities share.

total.description: The total column count the overlap was measured against.

oneOf.description: The two entities share a parent.
The two entities came from the same source system.

ExportPreview.description:
What an export would contain, without writing it — Phase 3 item 3.15's
preview. Counts, not the elements themselves: a reader deciding whether
a scope is too broad needs the size, not the data a moment before
downloading it.

edges.description: How many edges the export would contain.

nodes.description: How many nodes the export would contain.

FieldChange.description:
One field's before and after. `None` on either side means the field was
added or removed — distinct from changed, because a consumer reacts
differently to a dropped column than to a retyped one.

after.description: The value after, or `None` if the field was removed.

before.description: The value before, or `None` if the field was added.

JsonGraphEdge.description: An edge the way `GraphEdge` (`ui/src/api.ts`) consumes it.

JsonGraphNode.description:
A node the way the Epic 40 explorer's own `GraphNode` (`ui/src/api.ts`)
consumes it — not an invented shape. Field names and optionality
(`fullyQualifiedName` absent rather than empty) are copied from that
interface exactly, checked by reading the file directly rather than
guessed at, since the plan's own criterion is "asserted against that
consumer's fixture."

_graph.description:
Epic 7c's named-graph and transaction-time markers, additive to
`ui/src/api.ts`'s own `GraphNode` shape rather than replacing any
of it — a TypeScript consumer parsing this JSON ignores fields its
own interface does not declare, so carrying these two costs the
explorer nothing while still letting a caller that *does* care
(Epic 9a's own JSON Lines round trip, a diagnostic tool) tell a
derived or historical element from a current, directly-asserted
one. Absent, not `null`, when the underlying node never had either
reserved property set.

kind.description:
`null` when the label does not name a real `AssetKind` — the same
"stays in the picture as a bare node" reasoning `ui/src/api.ts`'s
own doc comment states for a node the reader may not fully resolve.

JsonGraphView.description: The whole document the way `GraphView` (`ui/src/api.ts`) consumes it.

Licence.description:
How a pack may be used — tracked per pack and surfaced (decision 3).

**No `Default` and no "unknown" variant.** A pack whose manifest omits
this must refuse import rather than be guessed permissive — see
[`crate`]'s module doc and Slice B's own acceptance criterion. Making
this required at the type level, not merely validated, is what makes
that guarantee structural rather than a check someone could forget to
call.

oneOf.description: Freely redistributable and usable.

Usable, but the notice must be surfaced wherever a term from this
pack is displayed.

Import must be explicitly acknowledged — see
[`import_requires_acknowledgement`].

LifecycleState.description: Where an asset is in its life.

LinkRelation.description: How a memory relates to what it is about.

Memory.description:
A piece of organizational knowledge.

**No staleness field.** Whether a memory still describes its subject changes
when the *subject* changes, not when the memory does — so a stored flag is
wrong the moment somebody edits the table it is about, and wrong silently.
See [`staleness`].

asOf.description:
The instant this was true of its subject. Compared against the subject's
version to compute staleness.

authorship.description: Who wrote it, and therefore how much it is worth.

confidence.description: How sure the author is, in `[0, 1]`.

kind.description: What kind of knowledge this is.

retractedAt.description:
When this memory was retracted, if it has been.

**Distinct from `superseded_by`.** A correction replaces a memory with
a better one; a retraction says the memory is no longer believed at
all, and there may be nothing to replace it with. Never a delete —
the same reason `superseded_by` is set rather than the row removed.

retractionReason.description:
Why this memory was retracted. Always present alongside
`retracted_at`, never alone: a retraction with no reason is one
nobody reading it later can act on.

summary.description:
A one-line form for a list or an agent's context budget. Optional: a
forced summary is a truncated first sentence, which is worse than none.

supersededBy.description:
The memory that corrected this one. **Set rather than overwriting**, so
what people believed survives being corrected — which is most of the
value of keeping a record at all.

supersedes.description: The memory this one corrects, if any.

MemoryKind.description: What kind of knowledge this is.

MemoryLink.description: One edge from a memory to something in the catalog.

relation.description: How this memory relates to the target.

target.description: The asset, run, or other memory this points at.

MergeDecidedBy.description:
Who — or what — decided a merge.

Deliberately not the shared [`crate::memory::Authorship`] type: that one
models a memory's author and has no notion of an automated decision,
while a merge's most common decider *is* the auto-merge band itself. A
third variant bolted onto `Authorship` for this one caller would make
every memory-authoring call site pattern-match a case that can never
apply to it.

oneOf.description: The confidence-band decision itself, unattended.
A person, reviewing the review queue.
An automated agent.

model.description: The model the agent ran on.

MergeRecord.description:
The reversibility contract (decision 1, `17-entity-resolution.md`): a
merge is a record, not a destructive rewrite. `split_at` turns it from a
live merge into a historical one without deleting the evidence that
produced it.

canonical.description: The entity that survives the merge.

confidence.description: The scorer's confidence in the merge.

evidence.description: Why the two were judged the same.

id.description: The stable identifier of this merge record.

merged.description: The entity merged into the canonical one.

mergedAtT.description:
The engine transaction time the merge itself wrote at — internal
bookkeeping, not part of the plan's illustrative sketch, but what
makes a split able to restore exactly the state `merged_at_t - 1`
(the moment just before the merge's own retraction) held, via
time-travel, rather than reconstructing it from wall-clock time
against a transaction log whose granularity was never meant to
answer that question precisely.

splitAt.description: When the merge was reversed, if it has been.

glossaryId.description: The pack-owned glossary its terms landed in.

packId.description:
A short slug ("fibo", "icd10") — not unique alone, since a pack has
several versions over time; `(pack_id, version)` is the real key.

OverrideKind.description: What kind of change a [`PackOverride`] makes.

OwnerKind.description:
What kind of principal owns something.

Deliberately **not** [`crate::PrincipalKind`], which answers a different
question — who is *calling* (User/Service/System). An owner is a person or a
team; a service cannot be accountable for an asset, because accountability
means somebody can be asked.

PackAttachmentCount.description: One pack term's attachment count — Epic 33 Slice E's removal report.

count.description: How many assets or columns carry this term.

sourceIri.description: The term's own concept IRI in the source vocabulary.

PackOverride.description:
An organization's local customization of one pack term — decision 2,
"extend without fork". Stored keyed by `term_path`, the term's own
**source concept IRI**, not its local database id: the id a re-import or
upgrade assigns is not guaranteed stable across storage adapters or
migrations, but the IRI is the one thing the publisher itself promises
not to change for the same concept.

PackRemovalReport.description: What removing a pack would affect, or did affect — Epic 33 Slice E.

attachmentCounts.description: Only terms with at least one attachment appear.

termCount.description: How many terms this pack has, whether or not any are attached.

totalAttachments.description:
The sum of `attachment_counts` — the number a caller decides on
without having to fold the list themselves.

PackUpgradeResult.description:
The result of an upgrade attempt — Epic 33 Slice D. `applied` is `false`
for a dry run, or when the diff found nothing to do.

applied.description: Whether the diff was actually written.

report.description: What differs between the installed version and the candidate.

Paging.description: How to fetch the page after this one.

after.description:
Token for the next page, or `None` on the last one. Nullness is the
only end-of-results signal a client gets, so it must be exact.

Post.description:
One message in a thread. Author is always the authenticated principal —
never client-supplied (Slice A's own trust boundary).

author.description: Who wrote it — always the authenticated principal.

deleted.description:
A tombstone, not a row removal — deleting must preserve thread
structure (Slice A's own acceptance criteria) rather than leaving a
hole a reply's `thread_id` still points into.

editedAt.description: Set the moment the author edits it — `None` means still as written.

threadId.description: Which thread this post belongs to.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Every error response uses this shape.

errors.description: Field violations, all of them — never just the first.

type.description: Stable URI naming the error kind. The only field a client should branch on.

Proposal.description: An agent's suggestion, awaiting a human.

baseVersion.description:
The entity version this was proposed against. A proposal against a value
that has since moved is stale — see [`is_stale`].

change.description: The proposed value, shaped by the capability.

confidence.description:
What the agent believed. Carried onto the proposal so a reviewer can
triage by it.

proposedBy.description:
Who suggested it. **Always the agent**, never the human who later accepts
— see [`accepted_attribution`].

rationale.description:
**Why.** Required, because a suggestion an agent cannot justify is one a
reviewer cannot evaluate, and a queue of unjustified suggestions is a
queue nobody works.

ProposalStatus.description: Where a proposal is in its life.

RateLimit.description:
How many writes an agent may make in a window.

**Per agent, per capability, per window** — not a global cap. A single
runaway agent must not be able to spend everybody else's budget, and a
runaway *loop* is usually confined to one capability, so a per-capability
limit stops it while leaving the agent's other work alive.

ReactionAction.description: What a toggle should do next.

ReactionKind.description:
A fixed, closed set — this project's standing answer to an open-ended
vocabulary nobody would ever finish arguing about. Not derived from any
external spec; named here once rather than as a bare string at every
call site.

Relationship.description:
A generic edge between two entities, named by kind rather than typed —
Epic 1's walking-skeleton relationship, predating [`Asset`]'s own
containment edges.

fromEntityType.description: The kind of the source entity.

toEntityType.description: The kind of the target entity.

Resolution.description:
What resolving one entity against its candidates decided.

Three variants, matching the three confidence bands exactly — `New` and
`Ambiguous` both leave the caller with **no** write to make, which is
the property Slice D's acceptance criteria are strictest about: an
`Ambiguous` that quietly created anything would defeat the review band's
entire purpose.

oneOf.description:
No candidate scored high enough to act on — including no candidates
at all.

Merged (auto-merge band) or already the same entity. `entity` is the
canonical id after the merge.

confidence.description: The scorer's confidence in the merge.

entity.description: The canonical id after the merge.

oneOf.description:
Review band: nothing merged, nothing created, and here is what a
human would need to decide.

candidates.description: The candidates a human would choose between.

ScopeRef.description:
What a grant is restricted to.

`None` on [`AgentGrant::scope`] means the whole estate, which is a real and
sometimes correct answer — but it is spelled as an explicit `None` rather
than an empty list, so nobody reads "no scopes" as "no access".

fqnPrefix.description:
An FQN prefix. `warehouse.retail` admits `warehouse.retail.public.orders`
and refuses `warehouse.finance.public.salaries`.

Table.description:
The pre-Epic-4 table entity — the walking skeleton's own type, kept
separate from [`Asset`] rather than merged into it (see `TableUpdate`'s
own history in the plans): a table created through this path never
projects into the graph.

createdAt.description: When the table was first created.

description.description: A human-readable description, if one was given.

fullyQualifiedName.description: The full dotted path from the root.

updatedAt.description: When the table was most recently changed.

TableUpdate.description: A partial update to a [`Table`]. Absent means "not declared".

description.description: The new description, if changing it.

name.description: The new name, if changing it.

Thread.description: A conversation anchored to an entity, optionally to one field on it.

about.description: The entity this thread is about.

createdBy.description:
Always the authenticated principal that started it, never
client-supplied.

field.description:
A field or column FQN this thread is specifically anchored to.
`None` means the thread is about the entity as a whole.

resolved.description: Whether the question this thread raised has been answered.

resolvedAt.description: When it was resolved, if it has been.

resolvedBy.description: Who resolved it, if it has been.

UpgradeReport.description: What upgrading a pack to a new version would do — Slice D.

attachedRemoved.description:
The subset of `removed` that still has assets attached — surfaced as
its own list, never folded into `removed`, so it cannot be silently
